body: @jianjin can you give some details on what not work and what you expect it to do ?

If an url like this : http://foo.com/images;num=10?query=name;value=123
the first ";" should not be replaced by &, because it is part of path but NOT query.
Host:foo.com
Path:/images
Path Parameter:num=10
QueryParameters:query=name  and value=123

The getPath() should be /images;num=10 but not  /images&num=10

https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/master/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/QueryStringDecoder.java#L117

^ that should probably only be applied to the query string instead of the whole URI

Yep. Or we could change the code @ https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/master/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/QueryStringDecoder.java#L225

to  (c == '&' || c == ';') {

Could you submit a pull-req ?

@jianjin @normanmaurer ,the ;in URL is just like &

see this:

```
According to the W3C: http://www.w3.org/TR/html401/appendix/notes.html#h-B.2.2

We recommend that HTTP server implementors, and in particular, CGI implementors support the use of ";" in place of "&" to save authors the trouble of escaping "&" characters in this manner.
The query string decoder that Netty provides follows this recommendation, which I think is reasonable. The best thing to do is probably to use a separator other than ; or URL-encode your data.
```

so 
localhost/get？key=a;b;c 
will make key=a ,and treat b and c as keys which will be null.
key=a
a=null
c=null
@jianjin I am wandering ,why you make you url pattern like that?
@hepin1989 Netty's decoder does it wrong at the moment, that's the issue here. Netty replaces ; with & in the whole URI instead of just the query string.

issue.title: [#1833] Replace ; with & only in the QueryString and not the whole URI
